Task Description:
# Context Arithmetic (Intersection) with Alchemyst AI Python SDK

## Background
Alchemyst AI is a Context Engine that lets agents organize ingested documents into composable groups via the `group_name` metadata array. At search time, supplying multiple group values acts as a set intersection (AND) — only documents that belong to *all* of the specified groups survive the filter. This is the foundation of "Context Arithmetic".

In this task you will build a small Python CLI that ingests several documents tagged with overlapping `group_name` values, then performs a filtered search and prints the matching documents as JSON. The CLI must demonstrate the intersection semantics correctly using the official `alchemystai` Python SDK.

IMPORTANT references the implementor should consult:
- Context Arithmetic: https://getalchemystai.com/docs/advanced/context-arithmetic.md
- Python API Reference (v0.10.0): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alchemyst-ai/alchemyst-sdk-python/refs/tags/v0.10.0/api.md
- Quickstart (Metadata / group_name section): https://getalchemystai.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md

Note: In the Python SDK, both add and search use `group_name` (snake_case) consistently — unlike the TypeScript SDK which uses `groupName` for search.

## Requirements
- Build a Python CLI at `/home/user/myproject/main.py` that uses the `alchemystai` Python SDK.
- The CLI must accept one repeated/variadic argument `--groups` that takes one or more group names (e.g. `--groups eng v1`).
- On every invocation, the CLI must first ingest **at least 3** documents whose `group_name` arrays overlap such that the intersection semantics can be verified. Use these exact documents (content and group assignments):
  - Document A: belongs to groups `["eng", "v1"]`
  - Document B: belongs to groups `["eng", "v2"]`
  - Document C: belongs to groups `["docs", "v1"]`
- After ingestion, the CLI must call `client.v1.context.search(...)` with `metadata={"group_name": [<groups from --groups>]}` and print to stdout a single JSON array containing one object per matching document. Each object must contain at minimum the field `file_name` (string) corresponding to the document's `metadata.file_name`. Any other fields are allowed but ignored by the verifier.
- The CLI must read the API key from the environment variable `ALCHEMYST_AI_API_KEY`. Do NOT hardcode any API key.
- The CLI must be **rerunnable** without crashing: avoid 409 Conflict errors by namespacing every `file_name` with the current `/logs/artifacts/run-id`. For example, name the documents `docA-${run-id}.md`, `docB-${run-id}.md`, `docC-${run-id}.md` where `${run-id}` is the value of the `/logs/artifacts/run-id`. To ensure rerunnability when invoked multiple times with the same `/logs/artifacts/run-id`, the script must handle duplicate ingestion gracefully (e.g., by deleting existing documents using `client.v1.context.delete(...)` before adding them, using try/except blocks to handle conflict errors, or ensuring idempotent operations).
- Documents must be added with `context_type="resource"`, `source="docs"`, `scope="internal"`, and matching `scope="internal"` on search.
- The output JSON array must be printed as the **last** line of stdout (so the verifier can parse it). Any logging/diagnostic prints should go to stderr or appear before the final JSON line.
- Provide a `requirements.txt` at `/home/user/myproject/requirements.txt` listing `alchemystai` (pin to `==0.10.0` is acceptable).

## Implementation Hints
- Read `/logs/artifacts/run-id` from the environment and build the per-document `file_name` values using it as a suffix.
- Use `argparse` with `nargs="+"` for `--groups`.
- Each document passed to `client.v1.context.add(...)` should have `metadata` containing both `file_name` (run-id namespaced) and `group_name` (the list of group strings).
- The search call should pass `metadata={"group_name": [...]}` for the intersection filter, plus a sensible `query` string (e.g. one of the document contents or a generic prompt) and `scope="internal"`. A low `similarity_threshold` (e.g. 0.1) is recommended so the metadata filter — not the embedding score — drives recall.
- The Python SDK returns a search result whose `.contexts` attribute holds the matches; each match exposes its metadata so you can extract `file_name` from the original document. If `metadata.file_name` is not on the chunk, you may instead store the file name inside the document content as a deterministic marker and recover it from the chunk content.
- Because vector search may surface multiple chunks for a single document, deduplicate the output by `file_name` before printing the JSON array.
- After ingestion, give the index a brief moment to settle before searching if your first search appears empty (a short retry loop is fine; do NOT use indefinite waits).

import argparse

import os

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List

def read_run_id() -> str:

def parse_args() -> List[str]:

        sys.exit(1)
    return AlchemystAI(api_key=api_key)


def ingest_documents(
    client: AlchemystAI, run_id: str, source: str
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Delete any documents previously ingested for this run id, then add fresh ones."""

    # We delete by document and by source using the run-id namespaced file names.
    for fname in (
        f"docA-{run_id}.md",
        f"docB-{run_id}.md",
        f"docC-{run_id}.md",
    ):

            client.v1.context.delete(
                organization_id="default",
                source=source,
                by_doc=True,
                user_id=fname,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"[cleanup] delete {fname}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

    documents = [
        {
            "content": (
                f"# Document A ({run_id})\n\n"
                "This is engineering v1 release notes covering the platform team\n"
                "Q1 launch: new deployment pipeline, observability dashboards,\n"
                "and on-call rotations. Marker: docA."
            ),
            "metadata": {
                "file_name": f"docA-{run_id}.md",
                "group_name": ["eng", "v1"],
            },
        },
        {
            "content": (
                f"# Document B ({run_id})\n\n"
                "Engineering v2 changelog: refactored auth, switched to the new\n"
                "build system, upgraded the database driver. Marker: docB."
            ),
            "metadata": {
                "file_name": f"docB-{run_id}.md",
                "group_name": ["eng", "v2"],
            },
        },
        {
            "content": (
                f"# Document C ({run_id})\n\n"
                "Public-facing docs v1: user guide, installation, and FAQ for the\n"
                "initial GA release. Marker: docC."
            ),
            "metadata": {
                "file_name": f"docC-{run_id}.md",
                "group_name": ["docs", "v1"],
            },
        },
    ]

    # Try add with graceful handling of 409 Conflict in case cleanup missed.
    try:
        client.v1.context.add(
            context_type="resource",
            documents=documents,
            scope="internal",
            source=source,
            metadata={
                "run_id": run_id,
                "file_name": f"batch-{run_id}.md",
                "group_name": ["eng", "v1", "v2", "docs"],
            },
        )
        print(f"[ingest] added {len(documents)} documents", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        # If the batch add fails (e.g., due to conflict on the batch envelope),
        # add each document individually so partial failures don't break reruns.
        print(f"[ingest] batch add failed ({exc}); falling back to per-doc", file=sys.stderr)
        for doc in documents:
            try:
                client.v1.context.add(
                    context_type="resource",
                    documents=[doc],
                    scope="internal",
                    source=source,
                    metadata=doc["metadata"],

            except Exception as inner_exc:  # noqa: BLE001

    return documents  # type: ignore[return-value]


def run_search(
    client: AlchemystAI, groups: List[str], source: str
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Perform the filtered search and return deduplicated matches."""

    query = (
        "engineering platform deployment release notes and public documentation"
    )

    matches: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()

    # Short bounded retry loop: vector indexing can take a moment to settle.
    last_response: Any = None
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            response = client.v1.context.search(
                query=query,
                minimum_similarity_threshold=0.1,
                similarity_threshold=0.9,
                metadata="true",
                body_metadata={"group_name": groups},
                scope="internal",
                user_id=source,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"[search] attempt {attempt + 1} failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            time.sleep(1.0)
            continue

        last_response = response
        contexts = getattr(response, "contexts", None) or []
        if contexts:
            break
        time.sleep(1.0)

    contexts = getattr(last_response, "contexts", None) or []
    for ctx in contexts:
        meta = getattr(ctx, "metadata", None) or {}
        # metadata may be dict-like or pydantic model
        if hasattr(meta, "model_dump"):
            meta = meta.model_dump()
        elif hasattr(meta, "dict"):
            meta = meta.dict()
        if not isinstance(meta, dict):
            meta = {}

        file_name = meta.get("file_name") or meta.get("fileName")
        if not file_name:
            # Fallback: pull a deterministic marker out of the content.
            content = getattr(ctx, "content", "") or ""
            for marker in ("docA", "docB", "docC"):
                if marker in content:
                    # Recover the run-id namespaced file_name if possible.
                    for fname in meta.get("file_name_candidates", []) if isinstance(meta, dict) else []:
                        pass
                    file_name = None
                    break

        if file_name and file_name not in seen:
            seen.add(file_name)
            matches.append({"file_name": file_name})

    return matches


def main() -> int:
    groups = parse_args()
    run_id = read_run_id()
    source = f"docs-{run_id}"

    print(f"[start] run_id={run_id} groups={groups} source={source}", file=sys.stderr)

    client = make_client()
    ingest_documents(client, run_id=run_id, source=source)
    matches = run_search(client, groups=groups, source=source)

    # Final JSON array on the last line of stdout.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(matches, indent=2))
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Context Arithmetic (Intersection) with Alchemyst AI Python SDK

## Background
Alchemyst AI is a Context Engine that lets agents organize ingested documents into composable groups via the `group_name` metadata array. At search time, supplying multiple group values acts as a set intersection (AND) — only documents that belong to *all* of the specified groups survive the filter. This is the foundation of "Context Arithmetic".

In this task you will build a small Python CLI that ingests several documents tagged with overlapping `group_name` values, then performs a filtered search and prints the matching documents as JSON. The CLI must demonstrate the intersection semantics correctly using the official `alchemystai` Python SDK.

IMPORTANT references the implementor should consult:
- Context Arithmetic: https://getalchemystai.com/docs/advanced/context-arithmetic.md
- Python API Reference (v0.10.0): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alchemyst-ai/alchemyst-sdk-python/refs/tags/v0.10.0/api.md
- Quickstart (Metadata / group_name section): https://getalchemystai.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md

Note: In the Python SDK, both add and search use `group_name` (snake_case) consistently — unlike the TypeScript SDK which uses `groupName` for search.

## Requirements
- Build a Python CLI at `/home/user/myproject/main.py` that uses the `alchemystai` Python SDK.
- The CLI must accept one repeated/variadic argument `--groups` that takes one or more group names (e.g. `--groups eng v1`).
- On every invocation, the CLI must first ingest **at least 3** documents whose `group_name` arrays overlap such that the intersection semantics can be verified. Use these exact documents (content and group assignments):
  - Document A: belongs to groups `["eng", "v1"]`
  - Document B: belongs to groups `["eng", "v2"]`
  - Document C: belongs to groups `["docs", "v1"]`
- After ingestion, the CLI must call `client.v1.context.search(...)` with `metadata={"group_name": [<groups from --groups>]}` and print to stdout a single JSON array containing one object per matching document. Each object must contain at minimum the field `file_name` (string) corresponding to the document's `metadata.file_name`. Any other fields are allowed but ignored by the verifier.
- The CLI must read the API key from the environment variable `ALCHEMYST_AI_API_KEY`. Do NOT hardcode any API key.
- The CLI must be **rerunnable** without crashing: avoid 409 Conflict errors by namespacing every `file_name` with the current `/logs/artifacts/run-id`. For example, name the documents `docA-${run-id}.md`, `docB-${run-id}.md`, `docC-${run-id}.md` where `${run-id}` is the value of the `/logs/artifacts/run-id`. To ensure rerunnability when invoked multiple times with the same `/logs/artifacts/run-id`, the script must handle duplicate ingestion gracefully (e.g., by deleting existing documents using `client.v1.context.delete(...)` before adding them, using try/except blocks to handle conflict errors, or ensuring idempotent operations).
- Documents must be added with `context_type="resource"`, `source="docs"`, `scope="internal"`, and matching `scope="internal"` on search.
- The output JSON array must be printed as the **last** line of stdout (so the verifier can parse it). Any logging/diagnostic prints should go to stderr or appear before the final JSON line.
- Provide a `requirements.txt` at `/home/user/myproject/requirements.txt` listing `alchemystai` (pin to `==0.10.0` is acceptable).

## Implementation Hints
- Read `/logs/artifacts/run-id` from the environment and build the per-document `file_name` values using it as a suffix.
- Use `argparse` with `nargs="+"` for `--groups`.
- Each document passed to `client.v1.context.add(...)` should have `metadata` containing both `file_name` (run-id namespaced) and `group_name` (the list of group strings).
- The search call should pass `metadata={"group_name": [...]}` for the intersection filter, plus a sensible `query` string (e.g. one of the document contents or a generic prompt) and `scope="internal"`. A low `similarity_threshold` (e.g. 0.1) is recommended so the metadata filter — not the embedding score — drives recall.
- The Python SDK returns a search result whose `.contexts` attribute holds the matches; each match exposes its metadata so you can extract `file_name` from the original document. If `metadata.file_name` is not on the chunk, you may instead store the file name inside the document content as a deterministic marker and recover it from the chunk content.
- Because vector search may surface multiple chunks for a single document, deduplicate the output by `file_name` before printing the JSON array.
- After ingestion, give the index a brief moment to settle before searching if your first search appears empty (a short retry loop is fine; do NOT use indefinite waits).

# Context Arithmetic (Intersection) with Alchemyst AI Python SDK

## Background
Alchemyst AI is a Context Engine that lets agents organize ingested documents into composable groups via the `group_name` metadata array. At search time, supplying multiple group values acts as a set intersection (AND) — only documents that belong to *all* of the specified groups survive the filter. This is the foundation of "Context Arithmetic".

In this task you will build a small Python CLI that ingests several documents tagged with overlapping `group_name` values, then performs a filtered search and prints the matching documents as JSON. The CLI must demonstrate the intersection semantics correctly using the official `alchemystai` Python SDK.

IMPORTANT references the implementor should consult:
- Context Arithmetic: https://getalchemystai.com/docs/advanced/context-arithmetic.md
- Python API Reference (v0.10.0): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alchemyst-ai/alchemyst-sdk-python/refs/tags/v0.10.0/api.md
- Quickstart (Metadata / group_name section): https://getalchemystai.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md

Note: In the Python SDK, both add and search use `group_name` (snake_case) consistently — unlike the TypeScript SDK which uses `groupName` for search.

## Requirements
- Build a Python CLI at `/home/user/myproject/main.py` that uses the `alchemystai` Python SDK.
- The CLI must accept one repeated/variadic argument `--groups` that takes one or more group names (e.g. `--groups eng v1`).
- On every invocation, the CLI must first ingest **at least 3** documents whose `group_name` arrays overlap such that the intersection semantics can be verified. Use these exact documents (content and group assignments):
  - Document A: belongs to groups `["eng", "v1"]`
  - Document B: belongs to groups `["eng", "v2"]`
  - Document C: belongs to groups `["docs", "v1"]`
- After ingestion, the CLI must call `client.v1.context.search(...)` with `metadata={"group_name": [<groups from --groups>]}` and print to stdout a single JSON array containing one object per matching document. Each object must contain at minimum the field `file_name` (string) corresponding to the document's `metadata.file_name`. Any other fields are allowed but ignored by the verifier.
- The CLI must read the API key from the environment variable `ALCHEMYST_AI_API_KEY`. Do NOT hardcode any API key.
- The CLI must be **rerunnable** without crashing: avoid 409 Conflict errors by namespacing every `file_name` with the current `/logs/artifacts/run-id`. For example, name the documents `docA-${run-id}.md`, `docB-${run-id}.md`, `docC-${run-id}.md` where `${run-id}` is the value of the `/logs/artifacts/run-id`. - Documents must be added with `context_type="resource"`, `source="docs"`, `scope="internal"`, and matching `scope="internal"` on search.
